tasks.title: Scaffold the afk TypeScript package with build and test tooling
tasks.objective: Create a buildable, testable TypeScript npm package in the afk project directory with no runtime dependencies and an exit-code constants module.
out_of_scope: Do not implement option parsing, prompt resolution, Codex execution, or the CLI entry point (src/cli.ts); later tasks do that.
Do not publish the package to npm.
Do not add runtime dependencies (the dependencies field must stay absent or empty).
Do not add linting, formatting, or CI configuration.
existing_context: All file paths in this task list are relative to the afk project directory, which is the `afk/` subdirectory of the Git repository root and already contains `specs/`, `.agents/`, `.claude/`, and `skills-lock.json`.
There is no application code, package.json, or tsconfig.json yet.
Local tooling observed when the tasks were written: Node.js v22.21.0, npm, codex-cli 0.162.1.
constraints: Run all npm commands from the afk project directory.
Use ES modules ("type": "module") and TypeScript module/moduleResolution "NodeNext"; relative imports in src must use the `.js` extension (for example `import { x } from './exit-codes.js'`).
Production sources live in `src/`; tests live in `test/` and are named `*.test.ts`; tests import production code as `../src/<module>.js`.
Only dev dependencies may be installed: typescript, vitest, @types/node.
Do not modify files under `specs/`, `.agents/`, `.claude/`, or `skills-lock.json` except the task list and progress bookkeeping allowed by the code skill.
implementation_guidelines: Create package.json with: "name": "afk", "version": "0.1.0", "description": "Run a Codex coding agent unattended, one task per fresh session", "type": "module", "bin": { "afk": "dist/cli.js" }, "files": ["dist"], "engines": { "node": ">=20" }, and scripts { "build": "tsc -p tsconfig.json", "typecheck": "tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit", "test": "vitest run" }.
Run `npm install --save-dev typescript vitest @types/node` so package-lock.json is created and the dev dependencies are recorded.

Create tsconfig.json with compilerOptions { "target": "ES2022", "module": "NodeNext", "moduleResolution": "NodeNext", "strict": true, "outDir": "dist", "rootDir": "src", "esModuleInterop": true, "skipLibCheck": true, "types": ["node"] } and "include": ["src"].
Create .gitignore containing the lines `node_modules/` and `dist/`.
Create src/exit-codes.ts exporting `export const EXIT_CODES = { success: 0, failure: 1, usageError: 2, interrupted: 130 } as const;`.
Create test/exit-codes.test.ts asserting each of the four EXIT_CODES values.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run typecheck` exits with status 0.
`npm run build` exits with status 0 and produces dist/exit-codes.js.
`npm test` exits with status 0 and runs test/exit-codes.test.ts.
package.json contains the bin entry `"afk": "dist/cli.js"`, `"type": "module"`, and no non-empty `dependencies` field.
EXIT_CODES equals { success: 0, failure: 1, usageError: 2, interrupted: 130 }.
`git status --short` shows node_modules/ and dist/ as ignored (not listed as untracked).
assumptions: The package name `afk` is a placeholder; the spec states npm name availability is unknown and publishing is out of scope.
Exit code 2 for input/option errors and 130 for user interruption are implementation choices; the spec only requires success versus unsuccessful/interrupted termination.
Vitest resolves `.js` import specifiers to the matching `.ts` source files.

tasks.title: Parse and validate afk command-line options
tasks.objective: Implement a pure option parser that returns validated run options or a clear option error message for invalid flags, limits, timeouts, and working directories.
out_of_scope: Do not decide which prompt source is used or read the prompt file or stdin; TASK-003 does that.
Do not print anything or call process.exit; return a result value instead.
Do not add options other than those listed in the guidelines (no --help, --version, or Codex argument passthrough).
existing_context: src/exit-codes.ts exists from TASK-001.
Node's built-in `parseArgs` from `node:util` is available; no argument-parsing library is installed or allowed.
constraints: Create src/options.ts and test/options.test.ts only.
Use `parseArgs` from `node:util` with `strict: true` and `allowPositionals: true`.
The function must be synchronous and must not write to stdout or stderr.
implementation_guidelines: Export `interface CliOptions { positionals: string[]; promptFile?: string; cwd: string; model?: string; reasoningEffort?: string; maxIterations: number; sessionTimeoutSeconds?: number }`.
Export `type ParseOptionsResult = { ok: true; options: CliOptions } | { ok: false; message: string }`.
Export `function parseOptions(argv: string[], processCwd: string): ParseOptionsResult`.
Declare string options: `prompt-file`, `cwd`, `model`, `reasoning-effort`, `max-iterations`, `session-timeout`.
Wrap the parseArgs call in try/catch; on a thrown error return { ok: false, message: error.message } (this covers unknown options and options missing a value).
Return all positionals unchanged in `positionals` (do not validate their count here).
max-iterations: if absent use 10; otherwise it must match /^[1-9][0-9]*$/ and be a safe integer, else return message `--max-iterations must be a positive integer, got "<value>"`.

session-timeout: if absent leave undefined; otherwise it must match /^[1-9][0-9]*$/ and be a safe integer, else return message `--session-timeout must be a positive integer number of seconds, got "<value>"`.
model and reasoning-effort: if present and `value.trim() === ''` return `--model must not be empty` or `--reasoning-effort must not be empty` respectively; otherwise pass the value through unchanged.

cwd: resolve with `path.resolve(processCwd, value ?? '.')`; use `fs.statSync` inside try/catch and require `isDirectory()`; otherwise return `--cwd "<value>" is not an existing directory` where <value> is the raw option value.
promptFile: pass the raw `prompt-file` value through unchanged (no existence check here).

Write tests for: defaults (no options gives maxIterations 10, cwd equal to processCwd, sessionTimeoutSeconds undefined), each valid option, `--` followed by a dash-leading prompt staying a positional, unknown option error, missing option value error, and each invalid value listed above (0, -1, 1.5, abc, empty string for numbers; empty/whitespace model and effort; non-existent and file-path cwd).
acceptance_criteria: parseOptions([], '/tmp-dir-that-exists') returns ok with maxIterations 10, sessionTimeoutSeconds undefined, and cwd equal to the resolved processCwd.
`--max-iterations 3` yields maxIterations 3; `--max-iterations 0`, `-1`, `1.5`, and `abc` each yield ok: false with the documented message.
`--session-timeout 30` yields sessionTimeoutSeconds 30; `--session-timeout 0` and `abc` each yield ok: false with the documented message.
`--cwd` pointing at an existing directory yields its absolute path; a missing path or a regular file yields ok: false with the documented message.
`--model gpt-x --reasoning-effort high` yields model 'gpt-x' and reasoningEffort 'high'; empty values yield ok: false.
`--unknown-flag` yields ok: false with a non-empty message.
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
assumptions: Session timeouts are whole seconds; fractional values are rejected as invalid.
A relative --cwd is resolved against the directory afk was started from.
Reasoning-effort values are not validated against a fixed list so that new Codex values keep working; Codex rejects unsupported values itself.

tasks.title: Resolve the launch prompt from exactly one input source
tasks.objective: Implement prompt resolution that accepts exactly one non-empty prompt source (positional argument, --prompt-file, or piped stdin) and otherwise returns a clear input error.
out_of_scope: Do not interpret, rewrite, or validate the prompt content (for example spec or task file references); return it unchanged.
Do not prompt the user interactively when no prompt is supplied.
Do not print anything or exit the process.
existing_context: TASK-002 returns `positionals` and the raw `promptFile` value without validating them.
constraints: Create src/prompt.ts and test/prompt.test.ts only.
Never combine sources and never silently ignore a non-empty source.
implementation_guidelines: Export `interface PromptStdin { isTTY: boolean; read: () => Promise<string> }`.
Export `type ResolvePromptResult = { ok: true; prompt: string } | { ok: false; message: string }`.
Export `async function resolvePrompt(input: { positionals: string[]; promptFile?: string; processCwd: string; stdin: PromptStdin }): Promise<ResolvePromptResult>`.
Export `async function readStream(stream: NodeJS.ReadableStream): Promise<string>` that concatenates all chunks and returns them decoded as UTF-8.
Step 1: if positionals.length > 1 return message `expected a single prompt argument but received <n>; quote the prompt`.
Step 2: if stdin.isTTY is false, call stdin.read() once and keep the text; if stdin.isTTY is true never call read().

Step 3: build the list of present sources in this order: 'prompt argument' when positionals.length === 1; '--prompt-file' when promptFile !== undefined; 'stdin' when stdin is not a TTY and the stdin text has non-whitespace content.
Step 4: if more than one source is present return `multiple prompt sources provided (<names joined with ", ">); use exactly one of a prompt argument, --prompt-file, or stdin`.
Step 5: if no source is present return `no prompt provided; pass a prompt argument, --prompt-file <path>, or pipe the prompt on stdin`.
Step 6 (prompt argument): if positionals[0].trim() === '' return `prompt argument is empty`; else return it unchanged.

Step 7 (--prompt-file): resolve the path with `path.resolve(processCwd, promptFile)` and read it as UTF-8 with `fs.promises.readFile`; on error return `cannot read prompt file "<promptFile>": <error.message>`; if the content trims to '' return `prompt file "<promptFile>" is empty`; else return the content unchanged.
Step 8 (stdin): return the stdin text unchanged.

In tests, build fake PromptStdin objects (isTTY true/false and a read function returning a fixed string, with a spy proving read is not called when isTTY is true); use a temporary directory for prompt files; test readStream with `Readable.from(['a', 'b'])`.
acceptance_criteria: A single positional 'build it' with a TTY stdin returns { ok: true, prompt: 'build it' } and stdin.read is never called.
A readable prompt file containing 'from file' with non-TTY empty stdin returns prompt 'from file'.
Non-TTY stdin text 'from stdin' with no other source returns prompt 'from stdin'.
A positional plus non-empty non-TTY stdin returns ok: false with a message naming 'prompt argument' and 'stdin'.
A positional plus --prompt-file returns ok: false with the multiple-sources message.
No sources with TTY stdin, and no sources with empty non-TTY stdin, both return the no-prompt message.
A whitespace-only positional, an empty prompt file, and a missing prompt file each return ok: false with the documented message.
Two positionals return ok: false with the single-argument message.
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
assumptions: Empty or whitespace-only non-TTY stdin is treated as 'not supplied', so `afk "prompt" < /dev/null` and use from scripts/CI work; a prompt consisting only of whitespace on stdin is therefore reported as 'no prompt provided', which is still a clear input error.

When stdin is not a TTY, afk reads it to end-of-file even if another source is given, to detect multiple sources; a caller that leaves a non-TTY stdin open without writing to it will block until it is closed.
A relative --prompt-file path is resolved against the directory afk was started from, not against --cwd.

tasks.title: Build the per-session prompt from the launch prompt
tasks.objective: Implement a pure function that appends fixed afk harness instructions to the unchanged launch prompt for every Codex session, including retries.
out_of_scope: Do not include any information from previous sessions, transcripts, iteration numbers, or retry state in the prompt.
Do not read task files, specification files, or progress files.
existing_context: The code skill's response protocol is defined in .agents/skills/code/SKILL.md under 'Coding loop protocol'.
constraints: Create src/session-prompt.ts and test/session-prompt.test.ts only.
The function output must depend only on the launch prompt argument.
implementation_guidelines: Export `const HARNESS_INSTRUCTIONS` equal to these lines joined with '\n': `---`, `Instructions from the afk harness:`, ``- Use the `code` skill to implement exactly one task for the feature described above.``, `- Follow the code skill's coding loop response protocol: your final message must be exactly one JSON object with an "outcome" of "repeat", "complete", "blocked", or "fail", with no other text.`, `- Nobody is available to answer questions or approve actions during this session.`.
Export `function buildSessionPrompt(launchPrompt: string): string` returning `${launchPrompt}\n\n${HARNESS_INSTRUCTIONS}`.

Test that the output starts with the exact launch prompt, ends with HARNESS_INSTRUCTIONS, mentions the `code` skill and all four outcomes, and that two calls with the same input return identical strings.
acceptance_criteria: buildSessionPrompt('Implement specs/x.md') starts with 'Implement specs/x.md' followed by a blank line and then HARNESS_INSTRUCTIONS.
HARNESS_INSTRUCTIONS contains '`code` skill', 'exactly one task', and the strings '"repeat"', '"complete"', '"blocked"', '"fail"'.
Calling buildSessionPrompt twice with the same input returns identical output.
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
assumptions: The code skill is discoverable by Codex under the name `code` in the user's prepared environment (spec Assumptions).

tasks.title: Validate the code skill's final JSON response
tasks.objective: Implement a strict parser that accepts a final assistant message only when it is a single JSON object matching one of the four code skill protocol shapes.
out_of_scope: Do not search for JSON inside prose, Markdown fences, or streamed activity.
Do not decide what action to take for an outcome; TASK-011 does that.
Do not read files or spawn processes.
existing_context: The protocol is defined in .agents/skills/code/SKILL.md section 'Response': shapes {"outcome":"repeat"}, {"outcome":"complete"}, {"outcome":"blocked","blocker_text":"..."}, {"outcome":"fail","failure_summary":"..."}.
constraints: Create src/protocol.ts and test/protocol.test.ts only.
The parser must be a pure synchronous function.
implementation_guidelines: Export `type ProtocolResponse = { outcome: 'repeat' } | { outcome: 'complete' } | { outcome: 'blocked'; blockerText: string } | { outcome: 'fail'; failureSummary: string }`.
Export `type ParseResponseResult = { ok: true; response: ProtocolResponse } | { ok: false; reason: string }`.
Export `function parseProtocolResponse(text: string): ParseResponseResult`.
Trim leading and trailing whitespace, then call JSON.parse in try/catch; on failure return reason `final response is not valid JSON`.
If the parsed value is null, an array, or not of type 'object', return reason `final response is not a JSON object`.
If `outcome` is not one of 'repeat', 'complete', 'blocked', 'fail', return reason `"outcome" must be one of repeat, complete, blocked, fail`.
For 'repeat' and 'complete': if Object.keys(value).length !== 1 return reason `"<outcome>" response must not include additional fields`.

For 'blocked': require typeof blocker_text === 'string' and blocker_text.trim() !== '', else reason `"blocked" response requires a non-empty "blocker_text" string`; return { outcome: 'blocked', blockerText: blocker_text } with the original (untrimmed) string.

For 'fail': require typeof failure_summary === 'string' and failure_summary.trim() !== '', else reason `"fail" response requires a non-empty "failure_summary" string`; return { outcome: 'fail', failureSummary: failure_summary }.

Write one test per accepted shape (including surrounding whitespace/newlines) and one per rejection: prose before JSON, prose after JSON, a ```json fenced object, empty string, a JSON array, a JSON string, unknown outcome, missing outcome, repeat with an extra field, complete with an extra field, blocked without blocker_text, blocked with empty/whitespace blocker_text, blocked with numeric blocker_text, fail without failure_summary, fail with empty failure_summary, and two concatenated JSON objects.
acceptance_criteria: '  {"outcome":"repeat"}\n' returns { ok: true, response: { outcome: 'repeat' } }.
'{"outcome":"complete"}' returns ok with outcome 'complete'.
'{"outcome":"blocked","blocker_text":"need creds"}' returns ok with blockerText 'need creds'.
'{"outcome":"fail","failure_summary":"tests red"}' returns ok with failureSummary 'tests red'.
Every rejection case listed in the guidelines returns ok: false with the documented reason.
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
assumptions: The spec forbids extra fields only for repeat and complete; extra fields on blocked and fail responses are accepted and ignored.
A whitespace-only blocker_text or failure_summary is treated as empty.

tasks.title: Build the codex exec argument list for one session
tasks.objective: Implement a pure function that returns the exact `codex exec` arguments for a fresh non-interactive session with automatic approval review, the selected workspace, optional model and reasoning-effort overrides, and a final-message output file.
out_of_scope: Do not spawn processes; TASK-008 does that.

Do not add any flag not listed in the guidelines, including --sandbox, --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, --json, --worktree, --ephemeral, --skip-git-repo-check, --ignore-user-config, --profile, or the resume/fork subcommands.
Do not read or write Codex configuration files.
existing_context: Installed codex-cli 0.162.1 `codex exec --help` documents: `--approve-for-me` (route approval requests through automatic review using the workspace-write sandbox), `-C, --cd <DIR>`, `-m, --model <MODEL>`, `-c, --config <key=value>` (value parsed as TOML), `-o, --output-last-message <FILE>`, and a `[PROMPT]` argument where `-` means read instructions from stdin.
constraints: Create src/codex-args.ts and test/codex-args.test.ts only.
Use long flag names exactly as listed in the guidelines.
The prompt must not appear in the argument list; it is sent on stdin.
implementation_guidelines: Export `interface CodexArgsInput { cwd: string; outputFile: string; model?: string; reasoningEffort?: string }`.
Export `function buildCodexArgs(input: CodexArgsInput): string[]`.

Return, in this order: 'exec', '--approve-for-me', '--cd', cwd; then '--model', model only when model is defined; then '--config', `model_reasoning_effort=${JSON.stringify(reasoningEffort)}` only when reasoningEffort is defined; then '--output-last-message', outputFile; then '-'.

Tests: exact array equality for (a) no overrides, (b) model only, (c) reasoning effort only, (d) both; and a test asserting none of the forbidden flags/subcommands from out_of_scope appear in case (d).
acceptance_criteria: buildCodexArgs({ cwd: '/w', outputFile: '/t/out.txt' }) equals ['exec', '--approve-for-me', '--cd', '/w', '--output-last-message', '/t/out.txt', '-'].

With model 'gpt-x' and reasoningEffort 'high' the result equals ['exec', '--approve-for-me', '--cd', '/w', '--model', 'gpt-x', '--config', 'model_reasoning_effort="high"', '--output-last-message', '/t/out.txt', '-'].
No result contains 'resume', 'fork', '--json', '--sandbox', '--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox', or '--worktree'.
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
assumptions: `--approve-for-me` is the Codex CLI flag that explicitly selects automatic approval review (verified against local codex-cli 0.162.1 help and the openai/codex source via Context7). It expands to the config overrides approvals_reviewer="auto_review", approval_policy="on-request", and sandbox_mode="workspace-write", and Codex rejects it together with --sandbox or --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox.

`model_reasoning_effort` is the Codex configuration key for reasoning effort, passed as `--config model_reasoning_effort="<effort>"` exactly as the official Codex TypeScript SDK does (verified via Context7).
Not passing --skip-git-repo-check keeps Codex's default behaviour, consistent with inheriting unrelated Codex settings.

tasks.title: Define session/run result types and status message formatting
tasks.objective: Define the session result, execution error, and run outcome types and implement pure functions that produce the exact terminal status lines and exit code for each case.
out_of_scope: Do not write to any stream or file; only return strings and numbers.
Do not implement logging to files or any persistent run history.
existing_context: src/exit-codes.ts (TASK-001) exports EXIT_CODES.
src/protocol.ts (TASK-005) exports ProtocolResponse.
constraints: Create src/outcomes.ts, src/report.ts, and test/report.test.ts only.
Returned lines must not end with a newline; callers append '\n'.
implementation_guidelines: In src/outcomes.ts export `type ExecutionError = { kind: 'launch-failed'; message: string } | { kind: 'exited-unsuccessfully'; exitCode: number | null; signal: string | null } | { kind: 'missing-response' } | { kind: 'invalid-response'; reason: string }`.

In src/outcomes.ts export `type SessionResult = { kind: 'response'; response: ProtocolResponse } | { kind: 'execution-error'; error: ExecutionError } | { kind: 'timed-out' } | { kind: 'interrupted' }`.

In src/outcomes.ts export `type RunOutcome = { kind: 'complete' } | { kind: 'blocked'; blockerText: string } | { kind: 'execution-error'; error: ExecutionError } | { kind: 'iteration-limit'; maxIterations: number } | { kind: 'timed-out'; timeoutSeconds: number } | { kind: 'interrupted' }`.

In src/report.ts export `describeExecutionError(error)`: launch-failed -> `failed to launch Codex: <message>`; exited-unsuccessfully with non-null exitCode -> `Codex exited unsuccessfully with exit code <exitCode>`; exited-unsuccessfully with null exitCode -> `Codex exited unsuccessfully due to signal <signal>`; missing-response -> `Codex exited without a final response`; invalid-response -> `Codex final response is invalid: <reason>`.

Export `formatIterationStart(iteration: number, maxIterations: number, isRetry: boolean)`: `[afk] Iteration <i>/<max>: starting Codex session` or, when isRetry, `[afk] Iteration <i>/<max>: retrying after execution error`.
Export `formatExecutionError(error)` -> `[afk] Execution error: <describeExecutionError(error)>`.
Export `formatTaskFailure(summary: string)` -> `[afk] Task failed: <summary>`.

Export `formatFinalStatus(outcome: RunOutcome)`: complete -> `[afk] Run complete: the code skill reported feature completion.`; blocked -> `[afk] Run blocked: <blockerText>`; execution-error -> `[afk] Run stopped after a repeated execution error: <describeExecutionError(error)>`; iteration-limit -> `[afk] Run stopped: reached the iteration limit of <maxIterations> without reported completion.`; timed-out -> `[afk] Run stopped: Codex session timed out after <timeoutSeconds> seconds.`; interrupted -> `[afk] Run interrupted by user.`.
Export `exitCodeFor(outcome: RunOutcome): number`: complete -> EXIT_CODES.success; interrupted -> EXIT_CODES.interrupted; every other kind -> EXIT_CODES.failure.
Export `formatInputError(message)` -> `afk: input error: <message>` and `formatOptionError(message)` -> `afk: option error: <message>`.
Write one test per output string listed above and one per exitCodeFor branch.
acceptance_criteria: Every string listed in the guidelines is produced exactly for its input, verified by tests.
exitCodeFor returns 0 only for complete, 130 for interrupted, and 1 for blocked, execution-error, iteration-limit, and timed-out.
formatFinalStatus for blocked includes the blocker text, for iteration-limit includes the limit number, and for timed-out includes the configured seconds.
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
assumptions: All afk status lines are written to stderr by callers so that Codex activity on stdout stays unmixed; the spec does not mandate a stream.

tasks.title: Run one Codex session and classify its result
tasks.objective: Implement runSession, which launches one fresh `codex exec` process with the session prompt on stdin, streams its output live, reads only the final-message file, and returns a classified SessionResult without leaving files behind.
out_of_scope: Do not implement session timeouts (TASK-009) or interruption (TASK-010).
Do not implement retries or iteration counting (TASK-011, TASK-012).
Do not parse Codex's streamed stdout/stderr for protocol JSON.
Do not set or modify environment variables for the child; it inherits afk's environment.
existing_context: src/codex-args.ts (TASK-006) exports buildCodexArgs.
src/protocol.ts (TASK-005) exports parseProtocolResponse.
src/outcomes.ts (TASK-007) exports SessionResult and ExecutionError.
constraints: Create src/session.ts, test/fixtures/fake-codex.mjs, and test/session.test.ts only.
Spawn with `stdio: ['pipe', 'inherit', 'inherit']` so Codex activity is displayed live and not buffered by afk.
Do not use a shell (`shell` option must be false/absent).
Always delete the temporary directory in a finally block.
implementation_guidelines: Export `interface SessionRequest { executable: string; leadingArgs: string[]; cwd: string; prompt: string; model?: string; reasoningEffort?: string }`. Production callers pass executable 'codex' and leadingArgs []; tests pass process.execPath and [fixturePath].
Export `async function runSession(request: SessionRequest): Promise<SessionResult>`.
Create a temp dir with `fs.promises.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'afk-'))` and set outputFile to `path.join(tempDir, 'last-message.txt')`.
Spawn `request.executable` with `[...request.leadingArgs, ...buildCodexArgs({ cwd, outputFile, model, reasoningEffort })]` and `{ cwd: request.cwd, stdio: ['pipe', 'inherit', 'inherit'] }`.
Attach `child.stdin.on('error', () => {})` to ignore EPIPE, then `child.stdin.end(request.prompt)`.

Wait on a promise that settles once: on the child 'error' event resolve to { kind: 'execution-error', error: { kind: 'launch-failed', message: err.message } }; on 'close' (code, signal) continue with classification.
If code !== 0, return { kind: 'execution-error', error: { kind: 'exited-unsuccessfully', exitCode: code, signal } } without reading the output file.

If code === 0, read outputFile as UTF-8; if the read fails with ENOENT or the text trims to '', return execution-error missing-response; otherwise call parseProtocolResponse and return { kind: 'response', response } or execution-error invalid-response with the parser's reason.

Create test/fixtures/fake-codex.mjs (starts with `#!/usr/bin/env node`, chmod 755) that: reads env FAKE_CODEX_STATE_DIR (required); reads `<state>/steps.json` (JSON array of steps); increments the integer in `<state>/count` (missing means 0) to get call number n (1-based); selects steps[n-1], or the last step if n exceeds the array; reads all of stdin; writes `<state>/call-<n>.json` containing { argv: process.argv.slice(2), stdin, cwd: process.cwd(), pid: process.pid }; if step.stdout is a string writes it to stdout; if step.ignoreSigint is true installs `process.on('SIGINT', () => {})`; if step.sleepMs is a number waits that many ms; if step.finalMessage is a string writes it to the path following '--output-last-message' in argv; exits with step.exitCode ?? 0.
In tests create a fresh state dir per test, write steps.json, set process.env.FAKE_CODEX_STATE_DIR, and call runSession with executable process.execPath and leadingArgs [absolute fixture path].

Test cases: valid repeat/complete/blocked/fail responses; exit code 0 with no finalMessage -> missing-response; finalMessage '   ' -> missing-response; finalMessage 'Done! {"outcome":"complete"}' -> invalid-response; exitCode 3 with a valid finalMessage -> exited-unsuccessfully exitCode 3; stdout containing '{"outcome":"complete"}' but no finalMessage -> missing-response; executable '/nonexistent/codex-missing' -> launch-failed; the recorded call has stdin equal to the request prompt, cwd equal to the request cwd, and argv containing 'exec' and '--approve-for-me' and not 'resume'; after runSession returns, the directory containing the recorded '--output-last-message' path no longer exists.
acceptance_criteria: A fake session writing '{"outcome":"complete"}' to the output file and exiting 0 yields { kind: 'response', response: { outcome: 'complete' } }.
A fake session exiting with code 3 yields exited-unsuccessfully with exitCode 3 even when it wrote a valid final message.
A fake session that only prints protocol JSON to stdout and writes no final message yields missing-response.
A non-JSON or prose-wrapped final message yields invalid-response with the parser's reason.
A non-existent executable yields launch-failed with a non-empty message.
The child received the request prompt on stdin, ran in request.cwd, and its argv contains 'exec' and '--approve-for-me'.
The temporary afk- directory used for the output file is removed after every runSession call, including launch failure.
src/session.ts spawns with stdio ['pipe', 'inherit', 'inherit'].
`npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
assumptions: Using `--output-last-message` is how the final assistant message is evaluated separately from streamed activity.
The temporary output file in the OS temp directory is transient session plumbing, not a persistent harness log, because it is deleted when the session ends.

tasks.title: Enforce an optional per-session timeout in runSession

tasks.title: Implement the iteration loop for protocol outcomes and limits

response/repeat: continue to the next iteration.
response/complete: return { kind: 'complete' }.
response/blocked: return { kind: 'blocked', blockerText }.
response/fail: log formatTaskFailure(failureSummary) and continue to the next iteration.
execution-error: log formatExecutionError(error) and return { kind: 'execution-error', error } (interim behaviour replaced in TASK-012).
timed-out: return { kind: 'timed-out', timeoutSeconds: config.sessionTimeoutSeconds as number }.
interrupted: return { kind: 'interrupted' }.

A fail outcome logs '[afk] Task failed: <failure_summary>'.
With maxIterations N, the runner is called at most N times, and a last-iteration repeat or fail returns { kind: 'iteration-limit', maxIterations: N }.
A last-iteration complete returns complete and a last-iteration blocked returns blocked.
timed-out and interrupted session results end the run immediately with the matching RunOutcome.
Each session start is logged as '[afk] Iteration <i>/<N>: starting Codex session'.

assumptions: sessionTimeoutSeconds is always defined when a timed-out result occurs, because runSession only times out when a timeout is configured.
